newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-TWIN STRIKE BY KULIK BOOSTS NEW-LOOK CSKA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWIN STRIKE BY KULIK BOOSTS NEW-LOOK CSKA.

text.p: Two goals in the space of three minutes by Vladimir Kulik secured an unexpected win for new-look CSKA against last year's Russian premier league runners-up Alania Vladikavkaz on Saturday.
In another match between Moscow rivals, champions Spartak comfortably disposed of Shinnik Yaroslavl 3-0 and head the table after the first two rounds of matches.

Kulik, former captain of Zenit St Petersburg, made his double strike shortly before the interval to provide some comfort for some 6,000 CSKA fans shivering in the cold at Moscow's open Dynamo stadium.
The pitch was cleared of 10 cm of snow with the help of troops hours before the kick-off.
Alania'a Ivan Getsko, who hit a debut hat-trick against KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny last week, missed a penalty in the first half but then scored from the spot in the 87th minute.

CSKA have a new look about them following the close season departure of coach Alexander Tarkhanov and much of his squad to Torpedo Moscow after a split sparked by the arrival at the army club of sacked Zenit St. Petersburg trainer Pavel Sadyrin.
A 14th-minute strike by Aleksei Bakharev put Spartak on the road to victory and second half goals from captain and playmaker Ilya Tsymbalar and Titov underscored their dominance.
Heavy snowfalls plagued many of the clubs and eight teams were penalised for not having installed under-pitch heating, being forced to play their home matches in southern Russia.
